params.condition: The two mechanisms can serve the same engineering function: they operate on compatible entities and quantities, accept compatible inputs, and produce interchangeable actions or outputs. Merely sharing a feedback pattern across unrelated domains does not qualify. Do not infer unstated interfaces. Use only the supplied excerpt; missing or unstated evidence means False.

params.instr: In 30-50 words list the input/output interfaces and operating assumptions that any substitute for this mechanism must preserve. This is a one-document requirement extraction, not a comparison with the joined document. Use only the supplied excerpt. Mark unstated fields UNKNOWN; do not invent performance results or claim scope.

Classify the primary intervention mechanism using exactly one label: FEEDBACK_CONTROL, SIGNAL_INTERPRETATION, RESOURCE_ALLOCATION, STRUCTURAL_CONFIGURATION, MATERIAL_COMPOSITION, PROCESS_SEQUENCE, or OTHER. Prefer FEEDBACK_CONTROL only when observation drives corrective actuation; prefer SIGNAL_INTERPRETATION for diagnosis without correction. Use only the supplied excerpt. Mark unstated fields UNKNOWN; do not invent performance results or claim scope.

Describe input -> decision or transformation -> output, the entity acted on, and its operating setting in 50-80 words. Preserve specific physical quantities and required interfaces. Use only the supplied excerpt. Mark unstated fields UNKNOWN; do not invent performance results or claim scope.

The excerpt specifies all three: an observed or predicted quantity; comparison with a reference, target, or loss objective; and adjustment of a physical control parameter or learned model parameter to reduce the discrepancy. Diagnosis, notification, display, or resource routing without a corrective parameter adjustment is insufficient. Return YES or NO. Use only the supplied excerpt. Mark unstated fields UNKNOWN; do not invent performance results or claim scope.
